title: A Bad Merge Is Deploying to Production Right Now
intro: Checkout started returning 500s two minutes after a PR merged to main. The pipeline auto-deploys main. A teammate suggests 'just git reset --hard to the previous commit and force push'.

steps.prompt: Identify the most recent commits on main.
steps.fake_output:
b7c8d9e (HEAD -> main, origin/main) feat: new pricing engine (#58)
a1b2c3d fix: typo in footer (#57)
9f8e7d6 release v2.4.0
steps.hint: Find the merge that lines up with when errors started.

steps.prompt: Revert the offending merge with a new commit — never rewrite main's history.
steps.fake_output:
[main 3e4f5a6] Revert "feat: new pricing engine (#58)"
 3 files changed, 8 insertions(+), 41 deletions(-)
steps.hint: revert creates an undo commit that goes through the normal pipeline.

steps.prompt: Push the revert to trigger the deploy pipeline.
steps.hint: A normal push — no force needed.

steps.prompt: Watch the deploy run to make sure the revert actually ships.
steps.fake_output:
✓ build   in 58s
✓ test    in 1m40s
✓ deploy  in 1m12s
✓ Run Deploy completed with 'success'
steps.hint: Confirm the rollback reached production before declaring it fixed.

resolution: The pricing-engine merge broke checkout; reverting it restored service in about four minutes through the normal pipeline. The teammate's suggestion (reset --hard + force push) would have been worse in every way: it rewrites shared history, breaks every clone that already pulled the bad commit, bypasses branch protection that usually blocks force-pushes, and leaves no record of what happened. revert is auditable, fast, and safe. When the fix is ready, the author can 'revert the revert' or open a new PR. Even faster options exist for later: 'kubectl rollout undo' rolls back the running deployment instantly without waiting on a pipeline, and feature flags let you turn off new code without deploying at all.
